Title: Copy Fabric
Content: Objective Copy and modify an existing Fabric in order to change Fabric properties partially. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Copy Operation Object Browser Select a fabric style to copy in the Fabric tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Copy A new Fabric item with the same properties of the selected Fabric item is now being created.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying and modifying the properties of an existing fabric in the Object Browser's Fabric tab.

Title: Add Fabric Information
Content: Objective Add Fabric information in the Property Editor. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Set a Fabric's properties in the Property Editor. Once the setting is done, click Save button at the top-right corner of the Property Editor to complete. Note: Type and Content fields have been added to the Property Editor. Enter the respective information in these fields (ver3.1.0).
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to add and save fabric information in the Property Editor, including the new Type and Content fields introduced in version 3.1.0.

Title: Delete Fabric
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Fabric styles from the Fabric list. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Delete The selected Fabric style is now being deleted from the Fabric list. Note: It can also be deleted by selecting a Fabric and pressing Delete key on keyboard. Fabrics can only be deleted when it is not being applied to any of Patterns.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to delete unnecessary Fabric styles from the Fabric list in the Object Browser, ensuring they follow the specified guidelines.

Title: Preview Fabric Information
Content: Objective Preview Fabric information in the Library window. Location Library Fabric Fabric File (.zfab) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Library Fabric Fabric File (.zfab) Preview of Fabric files is now being displayed below the Library section. Note: Only fabric files saved in Marvelous Designer 4 and above are allowed to display Fabric information preview. For any fabric files created in previous versions, need to be saved again in ver3.1.0 or above (ver3.1.0).
ContentDescription: This webpage provides instructions on how to preview fabric information in the Library window for files compatible with Marvelous Designer 4 and above.

Title: Open/Save Fabric File
Content: Objective Save a frequently used Fabric as a .zfab file or open a saved Fabric file to reuse. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Open/Save Operation Select a Fabric style to save from the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. Follow the indicated guideline below: Fabric Property Editor Open/Save The selected Fabric is now being saved, and able to reuse.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for saving and reusing Fabric styles as .zfab files through the Object Browser and Fabric Property Editor.

Title: Fabric Front/Back/Side Setting
Content: Objective Use this function to set different Fabric materials for the front/back/side of a Pattern. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Front, Back, Side Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Front, Back, Side Uncheck the Use Same Material as Front menu. Apply different materials to each side of the Pattern.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a guide for applying distinct Fabric materials to the front, back, and sides of a Pattern using the Fabric Property Editor.

Title: Fabric Texture Normal Map
Content: Objective Apply Normal Maps to express bumpy surfaces such as twill, corduroy, and leather. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map Operation Fabric Normal Map Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map An intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be adjusted with the scrollbar or entered directly. Depending on the normal map applied, the visual depth will change as you scroll from negative to positive values. Apply Fabric Normal Map Image Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Property Editor Material Normal Map Click on Open button. Select and load the desired texture image file. The selected image is now applied. Note : Although a Normal Map is automatically generated for Fabric textures, it is recommended to use third party solutions to generate more distinctive normal map effects. This feature can also be used to overlay a different texture above the existing texture. The normal map image size can also be adjusted via: Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Normal Map menu in the Property Editor (ver4.0.0). Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (ver4.0.0).
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on applying Normal Maps to enhance the visual depth of various fabric textures, allowing users to create realistic bumpy surfaces like twill, corduroy, and leather.

Title: Refresh Texture
Content: Objective Edit texture images with an image editing tool and save over the original image with the same name and file location, press Refresh button to instantly apply the changes of the Fabric's texture images. Location Main Menu 3D/2D Window Background Right-click Pop-up Menu Refresh Textures
ContentDescription: This web page provides a streamlined tool for editing and refreshing texture images directly within the 3D/2D window, allowing users to easily save changes and instantly apply updates.

Title: Desaturation
Content: Objective Use this function to maintain the texture of texture images or patterns while changing colors. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Operation Shadow Intensity Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Enter the Shadow Intensity value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. The Shadow Intensity is now being adjusted and applied. Shadow Brightness Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Texture Desaturation Enter the Shadow Brightness value directly or move the scrollbar to adjust. The Shadow Brightness is now being adjusted and applied.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a tool for adjusting shadow intensity and brightness in texture images while preserving their original patterns and colors.

Title: Edit Texture
Content: Objective Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D/3D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Move Follow the indicated location above. Click Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. Zoom In/Out Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to zoom in/out. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. Click Drag the diagonal line. Enlarge or reduce the size of the selected texture image. The selected texture image is now being adjustable while maintaining its horizontal and vertical ratios. Click Drag the horizontal line in order to enlarge/reduce the texture image to up/down and left/right. All texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjustable corresponding to the axis direction. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the image's Width and Height value in Property Editor Material Texture Transformation. The width and height of all texture images applied to the same Fabric are now being adjusted. Rotate Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. Drag around the circumference of the circle. The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being rotated. Rotate Grainline Follow the indicated location above. Click on a Pattern to rotate its grainline. The selected Pattern's grainline is now being in black color. Drag around the activated grainline, when the mouse cursor becomes in a shape of circular rotation. The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. Alternatively, select a Fabric and enter the angle value for grainline in Property Editor Fabric Grain Direction. The selected grainline is now being rotated and so as the texture image. Simulate once it is adjusted. The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. Align Grain Parallel to Selected Follow the indicated location above. Select a Pattern to rotate its grain. The grain of the selected Pattern is activated. When multiple Patterns are selected, only the last Pattern's grain is activated, but the configuration is applied to all Patterns. Right click on the Pattern and select Align Grain Parallel to Selected. All selectable segments are highlighted. Hover the mouse over the segment which the grain is to be aligned with. The segment is highlighted in light blue. The grain rotates. When the selected segment is a curve, the grain rotates based on a line connecting the ends of the curve. Click the desired segment. The grain rotates parallel to the selected line. When multiple Patterns are selected, all their grains rotate accordingly. Note: After selecting a Fabric, navigate to Property Editor Material Transformation Texture to type in the texture's width, height, and angle. Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. Edit back of texture when you change Garment Rendering Style as Back Texture Surface (ver. MD10)
ContentDescription: This web page provides comprehensive tools and instructions for modifying fabric grainlines and texture properties for individual patterns, enabling precise customization of garment designs.

Title: Apply Texture
Content: Objective Apply 2D image files to express the surface texture of fabric. Operation Via Drag and Drop Open a folder that contains the desired texture image in your file browser. Drag and drop the texture image onto a pattern in the 2D or 3D window. The texture of all patterns using the same Fabric will have the new texture applied. Note: If a texture image is already applied, the existing texture image will be replaced when applying a new texture image via drag and drop. Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Texture menu in the Property Editor (Ver. 4.0.0). Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (Ver. 4.0.0). After BaseColor Texture image is applied, maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1). If using a BaseColor Map with an alpha (to transmit transparency) and Opacity Map are applied at the same time, the alphas of both are reflected in the transparency result (ver.2024.1) Before (Ver. 2024.1) when the Basecolor Map and Opacity Map were applied at the same time: only the alpha of the Opacity Map was reflected in the transparency expression, not the alpha of the Basecolor Map. Now the alpha of both maps is applied (Ver. 2024.1) Via Property Editor Select a Fabric to apply a texture image to from the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. Follow the path: Property Editor Material Texture Open button. The Open File window appears. Find and select the desired texture image from the file browser, then load. The selected texture image is now applied to the Fabric.
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly apply and customize fabric textures using drag-and-drop functionality and advanced mapping features in our intuitive web application."

Title: Delete Texture
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary texture images as needed. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Right-click on the texture to delete. Click Delete Texture from the pop-up menu. The selected texture image is now being deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for deleting unnecessary texture images from the texture library.

Title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)
Content: Objective Use the Property Editor to resize the texture applied to the Patterns. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric (Select the Desired One) Property Editor Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric (Select the Desired One) Property Editor The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. Find the Transformation option which only appears when a texture is applied to a Pattern. Option Description Angle Type in the rotating angle. Width Set the texture width. Height Set the texture height. Lock Aspect Ratio Lock the width and height ratio.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Property Editor to resize and adjust the texture settings of Patterns in the Fabric tab.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
Content: Objective Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Buckling Stiffness-Weft/Warp
ContentDescription: This web page provides a tool to adjust the percentage of bending intensity used to determine the buckling stiffness of fabric corners, enabling precise control over fabric foldability based on user-defined parameters.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Friction Coefficient
Content: Objective Use this function to adjust the friction of Garments. The Friction Coefficient affects the friction between a Garment and another Garment. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset Friction Coefficient
ContentDescription: "Adjust the friction coefficient of garments to optimize their interaction and performance using the Fabric Property Editor."

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Density/Weight (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Use this function to express the weight ratio per unit (gsm). The higher the value, the heavier the fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset Density/Weight (Ver. 2024.1) Note: All versions before 2024.1 use "Density" in the Property Editor where Versions 2024.1 and after will use "Weight".
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a tool for calculating and expressing fabric weight ratios per unit (gsm), with updated terminology for versions 2024.1 and beyond.

Title: Show/Hide Texture  (Marvelous Designer 10 or earlier only )
Content: Objective Show or hide texture images as needed. Location 2D Toolbar Show 2D Textures Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Show 2D Textures The texture image is now being displayed or hidden.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a user-friendly interface for toggling the visibility of texture images in the 2D Toolbar.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
Content: Objective Use the Weft, Warp and Shear intensities to show the resistance against the horizontal, vertical and diagonal elasticity according to the 2D window. Increasing the Shear intensity to the same ratio as the Weft and Warp intensities, is going to express materials that creases easily such as cotton and denim. On the other hand, decreasing the intensity value is going to express more elastic materials such as silk and jersey. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
ContentDescription: This web page aims to illustrate how varying Weft, Warp, and Shear intensities affect the elasticity and resistance of different fabrics in a 2D window, enabling users to analyze material properties effectively.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Physical Property Preset
Content: Objective Some of the Physical Properties with detailed property values are adjusted beforehand as Presets for easier use. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with an accessible interface to easily adjust and utilize predefined physical property presets within the Fabric Property Editor and Object Browser.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Ratio
Content: Objective Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape, and then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset Buckling Ratio
ContentDescription: This web page serves to explain the Buckling Ratio, a metric that quantifies the bendability of various fabrics, helping users understand how different materials respond to applied force.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Internal Damping
Content: Objective Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. Note: Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference. Therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Internal Damping
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Internal Damping value to control the bouncing speed of garments in animation, enhancing their realism and movement dynamics.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
Content: Objective Use Bending intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately like the real fabrics. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Preset Bending-Weft/Warp Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive tool for adjusting fabric stiffness through Bending Intensity settings for both weft and warp directions, enabling users to accurately simulate the physical properties of various materials from rigid denim to flowing silk.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Physical Property Detail Setting
Content: Adjust each item of the detailed settings to express Physical Properties not included in Presets. Each property mutually affects one another and a Garment's physical property is expressed by combination of all detailed property values. Note: The property details are adjustable with the scroll bar or by entering in actual measurement values. Scroll Bar [0~99]: This is better input method when the constant value is far too enormous. To reduce this inconvenience, the most commonly used Physical Property is split into 99 stages. Constant Value [0~1000000000] This is better input method when setting far more accurate Physical Properties than the scroll bar method above.
ContentDescription: "Customize and fine-tune the physical properties of your garment by adjusting detailed settings with a scroll bar or precise measurement inputs, ensuring each attribute harmoniously influences the overall design."

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Rendering Thickness
Content: Objective Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as the default value, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. Note: To see the rendering thickness, the 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on Thick Textured Surface. Location Fabric Unit Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Operation Fabric Unit Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on setting and adjusting fabric thickness for garments in the 3D Garment window, ensuring optimal rendering visibility and style configuration.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Collision Thickness
Content: Objective Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. Location Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Simulation thickness property for garments to optimize collision limits and achieve smooth fabric simulation, including recommendations for form-fitting designs and skin offsets.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Open/Save Fabric
Content: Save a commonly used fabric as a PSP file and reload it to use as needed. At Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Fabric, press Save to save and press Open to load the saved Fabric data.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for saving and loading fabric data as PSP files using the Object Browser Fabric Property Editor.

Title: Opacity Setting
Content: Objective Adjust Opacity to express transparent or translucent materials. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Opacity Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Opacity Move the Opacity scroll-bar to adjust. Note: When the Opacity is at 0, the Garment no longer appears and becomes unable to select from the 3D window. It is recommended to set the rendering style to Show Thick Texture instead of Show Texture when checking invisible Garments.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides guidance on adjusting the opacity of materials to effectively visualize transparent or translucent garments in the Fabric Property Editor.

Title: Select All Sewn Patterns (ver. 12.2)
Content: Objective Makes it easier to select multiple pattern pieces that are connected by sewing relationships. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move tool Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern tool Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern tool (right-click on Pattern) "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" Main Menu Toolbar Edit "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" Operation Follow the dedicated path for the tool found in "Location" above. All patterns that are either directly or indirectly linked by sewing relationships will be selected. Note: - Select multiple patterns using Shift key. While holding down Shift key, double-click on a specific pattern or use right-click to open the drop-down menu on a pattern piece and pick "Select All Sewn Patterns" to select additional pattern pieces with sewing relationship while maintaining the pre-existing selection. -Piping, binding, buttons, interior shapes, and sewn objects are not selected with the Select All Sewn Patterns feature. -Patterns connected by zippers are selected together with the "Select All Sewn Patterns" feature. -At least 1 pattern piece must be selected for the hotkeys to work.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on efficiently selecting multiple interconnected pattern pieces using sewing relationships through various tools and shortcuts.

Title: 3D Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
Content: Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Free Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing. Note: 3D Sewing Video
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to create and manage Sewing Lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes in both 2D and 3D environments, ensuring precise and efficient sewing operations.

Title: 3D 1:N Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. Note While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Note: 3D Sewing Video
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for sewing multiple segments to a single segment in a 3D environment, ensuring accurate alignment and functionality through interactive visual aids and keyboard shortcuts.
